title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Targeted searches also support its narrowly stated gaps around node-specific administration, automation, identity documentation and pricing.

claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason, call tools and read knowledge before returning a result.

claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: Makers add a node through Copilot Studio > Workflows > workflow > Build > Agent on the Add panel.
claims.quote: In Copilot Studio, go to **Workflows** and open an existing workflow, or create a new one. Existing workflow: Open the workflow and go to the **Build** tab. Select the **Agent** icon on the Add panel.

claims.claim: The existing-agent option selects a published agent.
claims.quote: **An existing agent**: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its previously configured instructions, tools and knowledge.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow configures an inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape inside the node.
claims.quote: **New agent for this workflow**: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow. The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Workflows overview says exhausted environment prepaid capacity blocks new workflow runs until capacity is available.
claims.quote: Once you fully consume your environment's prepaid Copilot Studio capacity, new workflow runs are blocked until capacity is available.

claims.claim: Workflows already running complete normally when prepaid capacity is exhausted.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role able to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The tenant-draw setting is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: select **Licensing**. Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**. Select **Manage Copilot Credits**. Select the environment. Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate. Under **Capacity overages**, clear **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment allocation and its tenant-draw enforcement rule.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01"; Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request identifies Copilot Credits with allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId set to MCSMessages.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID `MCSMessages` and are managed through the `licensing/allocationsV2` operations of the Power Platform API.

claims.claim: allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity sets the number of credits allocated to the environment.
claims.quote: allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages" allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 }

claims.claim: An enforcementRules entry with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false disables tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote: The **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** option in the admin center maps to the `TenantPool` enforcement rule

claims.claim: The allocation API request needs authenticated authorisation.
claims.quote: $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The allocation request uses Content-Type application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: The example allocation body correctly nests environmentId under scope and allocation and enforcementRules under an allocatedEntitlements entry.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages" allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } enforcementRules = @( @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ) } )

claims.claim: Tenant draw is selected by default for eligible Copilot Studio environments without allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: A published environment-group tenant-draw rule makes the environment setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic allocation requests cannot override a published environment-group tenant-draw rule.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column.

claims.claim: Administrators can configure an individual agent's monthly Copilot Credit limit.
claims.quote: Select the agent, and then select **Set limit**. Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.
